title: Plausible Is Not Enough: Trust and Evidence in AI-Authored Pull Request Review
abstract: arXiv:2610.21144v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code review is where AI-authored pull requests (AIPRs) must earn reviewer trust before integration, yet it is unclear whether reviewers apply the same criteria used for human-authored pull requests (HPRs). We surveyed 239 practitioners from 31 countries using matched HPR and AIPR questions to compare trust, evidence requirements, and verification practices within respondents. Most respondents (64.9%) reported lower initial trust in AIPRs. They relied less on author track record and subsystem familiarity, emphasizing instead human prompter expertise and bounded change size. For approval, respondents more often considered their own reasoning through critical cases sufficient for AIPRs than HPRs (55.2% versus 28.5%), while relying less on test coverage. Overall, 61.1% reported higher evidence requirements for AIPRs, and the share who would block approval under residual uncertainty increased from 19.4% for HPRs to 43.9% for AIPRs. Respondent

translated_title: 看似合理并不足够：AI 撰写拉取请求评审中的信任与证据
translated_abstract: 代码评审是 AI 撰写的拉取请求（AIPR）在合并前必须赢得评审者信任的关键环节，然而目前尚不清楚评审者在评审 AIPR 时是否采用了与人类撰写的拉取请求（HPR）相同的标准。我们调查了来自 31 个国家的 239 名从业者，通过使用相互匹配的 HPR 和 AIPR 问题，在受访者内部比较了他们对两者的信任程度、证据要求和验证实践。大多数受访者（64.9%）报告称对 AIPR 的初始信任度较低。他们对 AIPR 较少依赖作者的过往记录和对子系统的熟悉程度，而是更强调人类提示者（prompter）的专业能力以及变更规模的受限程度。在批准与否的判断上，受访者认为仅凭自己对关键案例的推理便足以批准 AIPR 的比例（55.2%）明显高于 HPR（28.5%），而对测试覆盖率的依赖则有所降低。总体而言，61.1% 的受访者表示对 AIPR 提出了更高的证据要求，而在存在残余不确定性时会阻止批准的受访者比例从 HPR 的 19.4% 上升至 AIPR 的 43.9%。
tldr: 对 31 个国家 239 名从业者的调查显示，评审者对 AI 撰写的拉取请求普遍初始信任更低、证据要求更高，且更多依赖自身对关键案例的推理而非测试覆盖率来决定是否批准。
en_tdlr: A within-subject survey of 239 practitioners across 31 countries reveals that reviewers grant AI-authored pull requests lower initial trust and demand more evidence, relying more on their own reasoning through critical cases rather than test coverage when deciding approval.
